key_insight: Combining Fourier features, complex-valued learning, and physics-informed convolutional residual networks enables flow reconstruction across large measurement gaps and substantial noise.
engineering_relevance: The approach could help recover velocity, pressure, and vorticity fields when experimental measurements are sparse, noisy, or unavailable in critical wake regions.
method: Fourier features represent oscillatory and multiscale flow structures.
Complex-valued representations support coupled amplitude–phase learning.
Convolutional residual blocks enforce Navier–Stokes constraints.
evidence_signal: Tests cover Taylor–Green vortex and cylinder wake flows at Re=100, three severe gap geometries, robustness under Gaussian noise up to 20%, and lower errors than a conventional PINN on forced 2D Kolmogorov turbulence with 5% Gaussian noise.
watch_item: Validation is limited to the reported two-dimensional cases; performance on three-dimensional, higher-Reynolds-number flows remains unestablished.
paper_title: Fourier-Feature-Embedded Complex-Valued Physics-Informed Convolutional Residual Networks for Sparse and Gappy Noisy Flow-Field Reconstruction
